_comment: Known-stale evidence, waived explicitly rather than silently. .github/scripts/check_evidence_formats.py fails on any report whose recorded input hash no longer matches the committed input ('staleness is failure', klayout-tools docs/design-evidence-tiers.md). An entry here downgrades one such failure to a loud note -- and only that one: the waiver names the exact report, the exact check, and the exact stale hash. It SELF-EXPIRES: once the evidence is regenerated, the recorded_hash below no longer matches and the checker fails until the entry is deleted. Every entry must name a tracking issue. Waiving without one is a schema error, not a judgement call.

waivers.reason: This 0.3.0-minted report compared against the retired flat rhigh reference value (1919368.0 ohm = 1360*L/W). Issue #563 traced the 0.8.0 deck's +4.2% rhigh extraction delta (klayout-tools#2652 transcribes rhigh.sym's end term 1.6e-4 ohm*m and width offset -0.04 um) and updated layout/lvs_reference.py to evaluate the PDK's own symbol formula, changing RPU's reference value to 1999501.7 ohm. Verified live under klt 0.8.0: this cell reaches status match / error_count 0 against the updated reference. Stale until the DR-0016 backlog re-mint (#561) lands.

Issue #571's NWell-tap enclosure fix (TAP_NWELL_MARGIN_UM 0.1 -> 0.3, the deck's nwell.enclosing.nactiv.1 0.24um floor) regenerated bandgap_top.gds, which also carries in the pre-existing top-level routing refresh #556 drew and d64246eb reverted out of that PR ('revert top-level regen pending #558 re-baseline'). Re-extracting the refreshed layout under the installed klt reproduces #556's own branch mint byte-for-byte (sha256:eac7901aa439bb76...), and the NWell fix itself is proven extraction-invisible: a via-refresh-only layout with the old margins extracts byte-identically. Shipping that re-extraction, however, breaks the actively cited item-8 characterization inventory (dut[] pins bandgap_top.pex.spice sha256:63b9a850...), whose only sanctioned remedy is a new dated characterization report; the PEX re-mint therefore lands with that re-audit (the PEX re-runs tracked in #278/#275). The committed PEX evidence stays physically valid for the fixed layout: extraction does not read NWell, so no well-connected value changes. Waived until that re-mint lands; the entry self-expires when pex_extract_report.json is regenerated against the refreshed GDS.

Same deferral as bandgap_top's entry: issue #571's NWell-tap enclosure fix (TAP_NWELL_MARGIN_UM 0.1 -> 0.3, the deck's nwell.enclosing.nactiv.1 0.24um floor) regenerated bandgap_core.gds, and the PEX re-mint is deferred to the item-8 re-characterization the dependency checker's remedy requires (PEX re-runs tracked in #278/#275). The NWell fix itself is proven extraction-invariant (the fix only moves the well edge; re-extraction of a via-refresh-only layout with the old margins is byte-identical, and amp's full re-mint under the fix changed no extraction byte). The committed 0.6.0-era core extraction also differs from any current-tool mint by the rppd value-model drift (r 445.9 -> 479.6 per the 0.6.0 -> 0.9.x model change), so re-minting now would silently move the committed probe's reference extraction. Waived until that re-mint lands; the entry self-expires when pex_extract_report.json is regenerated against the refreshed GDS.
